sourceChecks.claim: Cloudflare DNS introduction describes name-to-address lookup followed by web server communication; DNS does not carry HTTP paths and address discovery cannot attest application readiness.

Route53 request-flow documentation explicitly shows recursive root/TLD/zone queries and cached nameserver/address shortcuts; RFC1034 grounds resolver and zone/delegation roles. Reserved hierarchy is clearly illustrative.
Route53 record documentation distinguishes IPv4 A, IPv6 AAAA and name aliases; RFC1034 states CNAME RDATA is a domain name, supporting subsequent target resolution and independent records.

RFC8767 permits serving stale expired data when refresh fails. RFC1034 defines TTL cache lifetime, so lowering authority TTL cannot rewrite old cache entries; the timeline and staged overlap follow directly.

RFC9520 distinguishes absence from failed resolution and requires failure caching. RFC2308 followup defines NXDOMAIN/NODATA and negative lifetime from SOA, supporting independence from a newly added positive TTL.

Route53 failover explicitly combines configured health checks with answer policy. DNS cache and connection reuse explain unequal HTTP load and delayed movement; reachable healthy spare capacity remains an application requirement.

RFC1034 resolver/caching/delegation model supports discovery dependencies and redundant authorities; HTTP500 classification follows separate HTTP response semantics already checked in this session, not DNS service health.

RFC4033 explicitly defines data-origin/integrity authentication and trust chain without confidentiality. RFC9525 primary followup says intermediate DNS names are not reference identities; HTTPS validates the originally requested service hostname.
